findings.evidence: "## Overview" header appears again after another "## Program Overview" header at the beginning
findings.fix: Remove the second "## Overview" section (lines 59-61) or rename it to something more specific like "## Benefits Administration Overview"
findings.violation: The document has two separate "Overview" sections, one at line 3-5 as "Program Overview" and another at line 59-61, creating redundancy and confusion about which is the main overview.

findings.evidence: the review takes longer because the manager who normally handles it is traveling; the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email.
findings.fix: Clarify this section to either explain the proper approval workflow for when the manager is traveling, or remove the comment about the backup reviewer not being informed.
findings.violation: This sentence describes an operational problem rather than documenting policy, and it is unclear whether the backup reviewer needs to be told or whether this is a description of a failed process.

findings.evidence: Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt.
findings.fix: Revise to "Completing the request requires confirming eligibility and uploading the receipt" or "To complete the request, employees must confirm eligibility and upload the receipt."
findings.violation: The sentence has an awkward parallel structure mixing gerunds with different prepositions.

findings.evidence: You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year.
findings.fix: Change to "Equipment must be kept in good working condition, and the benefits team may request a brief photo verification once a year" or "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition, and we may request a brief photo check once a year" for consistency.
findings.violation: This sentence shifts from "You" to "we," which is inconsistent with the document's tone and person. The rest of the document uses passive voice or third person ("the employee," "the benefits team").

findings.evidence: the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time.
findings.fix: Change to "the deposit happens to offset costs the employee already incurred" or simply "the deposit reimburses costs the employee already paid."
findings.violation: The phrase "at this point in time" is redundant and verbose when "already" suffices to indicate the temporal relationship.

findings.evidence: Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review.
findings.fix: Revise to "Finance reconciles requests against the reimbursement log each month. Payroll releases approved amounts after that monthly review."
findings.violation: The repeated phrase "stipend item" used multiple times in quick succession makes this paragraph harder to read and sounds repetitive.

findings.evidence: Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available to the employee.
findings.fix: Rephrase to "The home-office equipment stipend is available only when all three conditions above are met" or "Employees become eligible for the stipend only after meeting all three conditions above."
findings.violation: The inverted sentence structure is awkward and makes this policy harder to understand quickly.
